name: Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
history: The parish's red-brick Gothic church of 1857 was the first in the United States to be named for the Immaculate Conception after the dogma was proclaimed in 1854. The present church was begun in 1924 and dedicated on 20 May 1928. It became a basilica on 9 February 2008.
arch: An Italian Renaissance church by Maginnis & Walsh of Boston, based on the Basilica of St. Mary Major in Rome, built for $1.25 million.
features: Its Austin pipe organ, Opus 1522, was built in Hartford in 1928.

look.d: The columned front takes its cue from St. Mary Major in Rome.
Statues stand on the roofline above West Main Street.

fun: In the early days, a landlord threatened to evict his tenant if any more priests said Mass in his house.
journal: St. Mary Major's little sister in Connecticut, white and calm on the Green.

quiz.q: Which Roman basilica inspired the design?
